skill.name: performance-analysis
skill.description: Analyze Claude Flow swarm performance, detect bottlenecks, generate reports, and review optimization recommendations.
skill.summary: Guides Claude Flow swarm bottleneck analysis, reporting, and optimization review.
skill.author: ruvnet

security_audit.summary: No confirmed malicious behavior or prompt injection was found. The static alerts are markdown code fences, inline command examples, fixed report writes, and documentation links rather than active exploit paths. The skill still relies on local Claude Flow CLI workflows, so users should review command execution and automatic fixes.

remediation.issue: Sample script uses child_process.exec for CLI commands.
remediation.suggestion: Use spawn or execFile with fixed arguments, or present direct CLI steps instead of a reusable exec wrapper.

remediation.issue: Automatic fix workflows can change swarm behavior.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation, backups, and development testing before any --fix workflow runs.

remediation.issue: See Also links include absolute workspace paths under .claude.
remediation.suggestion: Replace absolute workspace links with relative repository links or public documentation URLs.

content.value_statement: Performance bottlenecks can slow Claude Flow swarms and make optimization choices unclear. This skill guides bottleneck detection, reporting, and safe optimization review.
actual_capabilities: Guides bottleneck detection for current or named Claude Flow swarms.
Explains performance report options for markdown, HTML, and JSON outputs.
Covers communication, processing, memory, and network bottleneck categories.
Provides sample MCP calls for bottleneck detection and task result review.
Shows CI and continuous monitoring examples for performance checks.
Describes optimization areas such as topology, caching, concurrency, and resource tuning.
limitations: Focuses on Claude Flow environments, not general application profiling.
Requires a configured Claude Flow CLI or MCP setup to collect real metrics.
Automatic fix examples should be reviewed before any changes are applied.
Performance gains depend on measured workload data and are not guaranteed.

use_cases.title: Investigate Slow Swarms
use_cases.description: Find likely causes of slow Claude Flow tasks and rank bottlenecks by impact.

use_cases.title: Add CI Performance Checks
use_cases.description: Plan repeatable reports, thresholds, and artifacts for pull request or release checks.

use_cases.title: Plan Optimization Work
use_cases.description: Turn performance data into prioritized topology, cache, concurrency, and resource changes.

prompt_templates.title: Find Current Bottlenecks
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner analysis for a current swarm.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the performance-analysis skill to identify bottlenecks in my current Claude Flow swarm. Summarize issues by impact and recommend review steps.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Weekly Report Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill to create a weekly performance report plan for a Claude Flow swarm. Include metrics, sections, and export format guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Swarm Performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill to compare current swarm performance with a previous swarm. Highlight regressions, improvements, and priority recommendations.

prompt_templates.title: Design CI Guardrails
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill to design CI performance checks for Claude Flow. Include thresholds, reporting outputs, and manual review before automated fixes.

output_examples.input: Analyze current swarm bottlenecks for the last 24 hours.
output_examples.output: A ranked bottleneck summary with communication, memory, and task queue impact. It includes recommended topology and caching changes.

output_examples.input: Create an HTML performance report plan for CI.
output_examples.output: A report outline covering executive summary, metrics, bottlenecks, comparisons, and recommendations. It also lists artifact and threshold guidance.

output_examples.input: Review whether automatic fixes should run after analysis.
output_examples.output: A cautionary checklist covering baseline data, development testing, incremental changes, and post-change monitoring.

best_practices: Run analysis after major topology, cache, or agent changes.
Review generated recommendations before applying automatic fixes.
Store reports with consistent time ranges so trends are comparable.
anti_patterns: Running automatic fixes on production swarms without a recent backup or review.
Comparing reports that use different time ranges or thresholds.
Treating sample performance gains as guaranteed results.

faq.question: What systems does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Claude Flow swarms and related agent performance workflows.

faq.question: Does it collect measurements by itself?
faq.answer: No. It guides CLI and MCP workflows that require a configured Claude Flow environment.

faq.question: Can it automatically fix bottlenecks?
faq.answer: It documents automatic fix workflows, but users should review changes before applying them.

faq.question: Which report formats are covered?
faq.answer: The skill covers markdown, HTML, and JSON report workflows.

faq.question: Is it useful for CI/CD?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for performance reports, thresholds, and uploaded artifacts.

faq.question: What permissions should users review?
faq.answer: Users should review CLI execution, report output paths, and any automatic optimization step.
